title: Patient Identification
std_title: GSR.01 Accurate patient identification through at least two identifiers to identify the
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy and procedure for patient identification that addresses all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through f).
All healthcare professionals are aware of hospital policy.
Patient identification is conducted before performing diagnostic procedures, providing treatments, and performing any procedures.
The patient's identifiers are recorded in the patient’s medical record.
The hospital monitors the reported data on patients’ identification and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Verbal and Telephone Orders
std_title: GSR.02 Verbal or telephone orders are communicated and documented according to the
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy guiding the communication of verbal and telephone orders that addresses at least all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through e).
Healthcare professionals are aware of the elements of the policy.
All verbal and telephone orders are documented, then read back by the receiver, and confirmed by the ordering physician.
All verbal and telephone orders are recorded in the patient’s medical record within a predefined timeframe.
The hospital monitors the reported data of verbal and telephone orders and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Critical Results
std_title: GSR.03 Critical results are communicated in time and documented according to the
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy to guide critical results communications that address at least all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through d).
Healthcare professionals are aware of the elements of the policy.
All critical results are recorded within a predefined timeframe, including all elements in the intent from i) through vii).
The hospital monitors the reported data on critical results and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Handover Communication
std_title: GSR.04 A standardized approach to handover communications, including an opportunity
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through f).
All healthcare professionals are aware of hospital policy.
Handover communication conducted between different shifts and between different levels of care (different departments/ services).
Handover communications are documented using an established tool or format and are accessible as needed.
The hospital monitors the reported data on handover communication and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Fall Assessment and Prevention
std_title: GSR.05 Patient’s risk of falling is assessed, periodically reassessed, and managed.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy to guide the assessment of a patient’s risk of fall that includes all elements in the intent from a) through g).
Healthcare professionals are aware of the elements of approved policy.
The hospital assesses and reassesses all inpatients for risk of fall using appropriate tools suitable for the patient population and documented in the patient's medical records.
Outpatients with certain conditions, situations, or locations will be screened for risk of falls.
The families of patients who are at higher risk of falling are aware of and involved in fall prevention measures.
General measures and tailored care plans are recorded in the patient’s medical record.

title: Pressure Ulcers Prevention
std_title: GSR.06 The Patient’s risk of developing pressure ulcers is assessed, periodically
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy to guide pressure ulcer risk assessment that addresses all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through f).
Healthcare professionals are aware of the elements of the pressure ulcer risk assessment and of prevention measures.
The hospital assesses upon admission and reassesses each patient's risk for developing a pressure ulcer using appropriate tools suitable for the patient population.
The families of patients at higher risk of pressure ulceration are aware of and involved in prevention measures.
General measures and tailored care plans are recorded in the patient’s medical record.

title: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis
std_title: GSR.07 Patient’s risk of developing venous thromboembolism (deep venous thrombosis
eoc: The hospital has an approved guideline for assessment and management of patient’s VTE risk that addresses all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through e).
Healthcare professionals are aware of the elements of the VTE assessment process and of prevention measures.
VTE risk assessments are completed and recorded within an approved timeframe.
The families of patients at higher risk for VTE are aware of and involved in prevention measures.
Tailored care plans based on individual patient VTE risk assessments are conducted and recorded in the patient files.

title: Critical Alarms
std_title: The hospital has an approved policy and procedures for the management and use of clinical alarms.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) through e).
Competent individuals are responsible for the management and use of critical alarms.
Management and use of critical alarms are done according to the approved policy.
Management and use of critical alarms are recorded according to policy.
Alarm events and malfunctions are reported, and actions are taken to maintain the safety of clinical alarms.

title: Catheter and Tube Misconnections
std_title: A system is in place to prevent catheter and tubing misconnections.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) through e).
Competent individuals are responsible for the management and use of tubes and catheters.
Management and use of tubes and catheters are done as per the hospital policy.
Management and use of tubes and catheters are recorded in patient medical records.

title: Recognition and Response to Clinical Deterioration
std_title: GSR.10 The hospital has a hospital-wide process for recognition of and response to
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) through g).
All staff members involved in direct patient care are trained on recognition of and response to clinical deterioration.
Recognition and response to clinical deterioration are done as per the hospital policy, using age specific criteria.
Recognition and response to clinical deterioration are recorded in the patient’s medical record.

title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
std_title: Response to cardio-pulmonary arrest in the hospital is managed for both adult and pediatric patients.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) through i).
All staff members involved in cardiopulmonary resuscitation are aware of the hospital policy.
Staff with basic life support start the process immediately, while those with advanced life support will start within a maximum of 5 minutes.
Age-appropriate emergency equipment, medications, and supplies are available throughout the hospital.
Emergency equipment and supplies are checked daily and replaced after use.
Management of cardio-pulmonary arrests is recorded in the patient's medical record.

title: Radiation Safety Program
std_title: Radiation safety program is developed and implemented.
eoc: The hospital has a written, updated, and approved radiation safety program that addresses all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through h).
Staff members involved in medical imaging are aware of the radiation safety program.
The hospital ensures that exposed patients do not exceed the approved maximum level.
Environmental radiation safety measures, personal monitoring devices results, and the regular CBC results are available and documented.
Nuclear medicine safety measures are implemented by addressing the elements from i) through v) in the intent.
Laser safety measures are implemented by addressing the elements from I) to III) in the intent.

title: Laboratory Safety Program
std_title: GSR.13 A comprehensive documented laboratory safety program is implemented.
eoc: A written updated program that describes safety measures for laboratory services and facilities is documented and includes the items in the intent from a) to j).
Laboratory staff are trained on the safety program.
Laboratory risk assessment is performed, and safety reports are issued at least semi-annually to the hospital environment and facility safety committee.
Spill kits, safety showers and eye washes are available, functioning and tested.
Safety precautions are implemented.
The hospital monitors the reported data on laboratory safety program and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Surgical Site Marking
std_title: GSR.14 The precise site where surgery or invasive procedure shall be performed is clearly
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy guiding the site marking process that includes at least elements from a) through g) mentioned in the intent.
Involved staff are aware of the implementation of site marking.
Site marking is a unified mark throughout the hospital and is performed by the physician responsible for the surgery or invasive procedure.
Site marking is performed before sending the patient to the operating room, involving the patient and the patient’s family.
The hospital monitors the reported data regarding the site marking process and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Pre-operative Checklist
std_title: GSR.15 Documents and equipment needed for procedures, anesthesia, or sedation are
eoc: The hospital has a process for preoperative verification of all needed documents and equipment.
The staff involved are trained on the hospital process for preoperative verification.
Recorded evidence of preoperative verification of all items mentioned in the intent before each surgery or invasive procedure exists.
The hospital monitors the reported data on the preoperative verification process and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Time-out / Sign-out
std_title: GSR.16 Time-out is conducted before starting surgical and invasive procedures, and
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy to ensure the correct patient, procedure, and body part before surgical or invasive procedures.
Time out is done immediately before surgery or invasive procedure starts.
Sign-out is conducted at the end of all surgical and invasive procedures and before leaving the operating location.
The hospital monitors the reported data on time-out and sign-out processes and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Instrument Retention Prevention
std_title: GSR.17 The accuracy of counting sponges, needles, and instruments pre- and post-
eoc: The hospital has a process to manage surgical counts.
Two staff members count sponges, needles, towels, or instruments before, during, and after the surgery or invasive procedure, as the second one acts as a witness for the first one.
The preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative counts are recorded, and the performing physician signs the record.
There is a process to manage and deal with miscounts once identified.
The hospital monitors the reported data on the counting process and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Medication Reconciliation (BPMH)
std_title: GSR.18 Medications are reconciled across all interfaces of care in the hospital.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy for medication reconciliation that includes all elements mentioned in the intent from a) through d).
Staff responsible for reconciling medications are trained to take the best possible medication history (BPMH) and reconcile medications.
Medication reconciliation occurs in situations mentioned in the intent from i) to iv) within a defined timeframe.
Medication prescribers compare the list of current medications with the list of medications to be prescribed and make clinical decisions based on the comparison.
Reconciled medications are clearly recorded, and related information is clearly communicated to healthcare professionals involved in the patient’s medication prescribing.

title: Medication Storage and Labelling
std_title: GSR.19 Medications are stored in a manner that maintains the security and quality of the
eoc: Medications are safely and securely stored according to the manufacturer/marketing authorization holder's recommendations and kept clean and organized.
The hospital has an approved process for the use and storage of multi-dose medications to ensure their stability and safety.
The hospital has a clear process to deal with an electric power outage to ensure the integrity of any affected medications before use.
Medications in stores, pharmacies, and patient care areas are periodically (at least monthly) inspected to confirm compliance with proper storage conditions.

Medications, medication containers, other solutions, and the components used in their preparation are clearly labeled (if not clearly shown in the original packages or boxes) with the name, concentration/ strength, expiration date, batch number, and any applicable warnings.

title: High-Alert Medications and Concentrated Electrolytes
std_title: GSR.20 High-Alert medications and concentrated electrolytes are identified, stored, and
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all elements from a) through c) in the intent
The hospital has an approved and annually updated list(s) of high-alert medications and concentrated electrolytes.
The hospital implements process(es) to prevent inadvertent use of high-alert medications and concentrated electrolytes.
The hospital trains healthcare professionals involved in the management and use of high-alert medications and concentrated electrolytes.
The hospital monitors the reported data on the management of high-alert medications and concentrated electrolytes and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Look-alike and Sound-alike Medications
std_title: GSR.21 Look-alike and sound-alike medications are identified and stored in a manner
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that addresses all elements from a) to d) in the intent.
There is an approved list of LASA medications that is updated at least annually.
The hospital provides training to the healthcare professionals involved in the management and use of LASA.
LASA medications are stored, segregated, and labeled safely and uniformly in all locations.
The hospital monitors the reported data on the management of LASA and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Hand Hygiene
std_title: GSR.22 professional hand hygiene guidelines are adopted and implemented throughout the
eoc: The hospital has approved Hand Hygiene policies and procedures based on current professional guidelines that address all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) to g).
Healthcare professionals are trained on these policies and procedures.
Hand hygiene is implemented according to the policy.
Hand hygiene posters are displayed in required areas.
Hand hygiene facilities are present in the required numbers and places.
The hospital monitors the reported data on the hand hygiene process and takes actions to control or improve the process as appropriate.

title: Fire and Smoke Safety
std_title: GSR.23 Fire and smoke safety plan addresses prevention, early detection, response, and
eoc: The hospital has an approved and updated fire and smoke safety plan that includes all elements from a) through f) in the intent.
The hospital provides training on fire safety and evacuation for all staff at least annually.
The hospital fire alarm and smoke containment system is available, accessible and functioning.
The hospital firefighting systems are available, accessible and functioning.
Inspection, maintenance and testing of fire alarms, firefighting, and smoke containment systems are performed and recorded.
The evacuation path is clearly marked with exit signs and free from obstructions.

title: Fire Drills
std_title: GSR.24 Fire drills are performed in different clinical and non-clinical areas.
eoc: Fire drills are performed at least quarterly, including one unannounced drill annually.
All staff members participate in fire drills at least once annually.
Fire drill results are recorded, including items from a) through d) that are mentioned in the intent.
Fire drill evaluation is performed after performing each drill with a corrective action plan when indicated.
The hospital staff guarantees a safe evacuation for patients, staff, and visitors.

title: Hazardous Materials Safety
std_title: GSR.25 The hospital plans safe handling, storage, usage, and transportation of hazardous
eoc: The hospital has an approved and updated hazardous material and waste management plan that addresses all elements from a) through k) in the intent.
The hospital ensures the availability of the hospital SDS.
Staff is trained on hazardous material and waste management plans.
The hospital ensures the safe use, handling, storage, and labeling of hazardous materials.
The hospital ensures that waste handling, storage, and labeling are according to laws and regulations.
The hospital has an approved document for spill management, Investigation, and recording of different incidents related to hazardous materials.

title: Safety Management Plan
std_title: GSR.26 A safe work environment plan addresses high-risk areas, procedures, risk mitigation
eoc: The hospital has an approved and updated plan to ensure a safe work environment, including all elements from a) through h) in the intent.
Safety instructions are posted in all high-risk areas.
Staff are aware of safety measures based on their job hazards.
PPEs are available and used whenever indicated.
Safety measures are implemented in all areas.

title: Medical Equipment Plan
std_title: GSR.27 Medical equipment plan ensures selection, inspection, testing, maintenance, and
eoc: The hospital has an approved and updated medical equipment management plan that addresses all elements from a) through c) in the intent.
The hospital has a qualified individual to oversee medical equipment management.
The hospital ensures that only trained and competent staff handles the specialized equipment(s).
Records are maintained for medical equipment inventory, user training, equipment identification cards, company emergency contact, and testing on installation.
Records are maintained for medical equipment, periodic preventive maintenance, calibration, and malfunction history.
Equipment adverse incidents are reported, and actions are taken.

title: Utilities Management Plan
std_title: GSR.28 Essential utility plan addresses regular inspection, maintenance, testing, and repair.
eoc: The hospital has an approved and updated plan for utility management that includes items a) through l) in the intent.
The hospital has trained staff members to oversee utility management.
The hospital utility management plan is implemented.
Records are maintained for utility systems inventory, testing, periodic preventive maintenance, and malfunction history.
Critical utility systems are identified, and backup availability is ensured.

title: Abbreviations
std_title: GSR.29 The hospital defines standardized symbols and abbreviations.
eoc: The hospital has an approved policy that includes all the elements in the intent from a) through d).
All staff who record in the patient’s medical record are aware of the policy requirements.
Symbols and abbreviations, including the approved list, are used according to the policy.
Violation of the list of not-to-use symbols/abbreviations is monitored, and corrective actions are taken.
